rationale.usefulness: Copilot availability and a defined routine-coding scope provide a useful route to evaluate accepted-patch cost. The original education, app, website and media-script examples have inputs, checks and failure conditions. Price schedules, plan eligibility and standalone deployment remain insufficiently established for a stronger actionable-value score.
rationale.impact: The potential contribution is meaningful competition on ordinary enterprise coding costs rather than a demonstrated field-wide capability break. The launch comparisons use specified harnesses and a 50% promotion; the report preserves those limitations. Impact 6 is consistent with the frozen 1,947-word body falling within the 1,800–2,200 band, subject to the final mean.
rationale.novelty: Task-focused price/performance and the Code 2/Flash division offer moderate differentiation. Neither the hosted model page nor vendor evaluations establish a fundamentally new technique, and customized MAI Work Flash/customer variants are correctly separated.
rationale.maturity: The announcement establishes availability in Copilot and a limited Foundry preview for Flash. The deliberate exclusion of very long-horizon work and unknown account, pricing and context details limit readiness; benchmarks and customer quotations are not treated as a reliability guarantee.
rationale.openness: Public launch material and model/data-card links permit limited inspection, but exact-model weights, licensing and reproducibility are unestablished. Future provider plans do not yet demonstrate portability. The report correctly avoids inferring rights from the wider Microsoft model programme.
